turns.user: My brakes have been squealing for a few weeks
turns.text:
I'm seeing your brakes are flagged as on-time based on your records — they were serviced about two months ago. That said, first-stop brake squeal is a pattern worth understanding before we move forward, because it can mean a few different things.

Here's what typically produces that sound: when brake pads wear down, manufacturers include a small metal wear indicator tab that intentionally contacts the rotor to create that squeal — it's basically the pad saying "hey, I'm getting thin, replace me soon." But squealing can also come from other sources: new pads sometimes make noise during a bedding-in period after installation (which can last a few weeks), glazed rotors, dust or debris trapped between the pad and rotor, or occasionally a loose caliper or pad shim. So the squeal itself doesn't automatically tell us which of those is happening.

Here's the key narrowing question: when you apply the brakes, does the squeal happen mostly just at the very beginning of the stop and then fade out — or does it stick around through the whole braking event? That distinction tells us a lot about whether this is normal pad break-in, wear indicators kicking in, or something less common that deserves a closer look.
